entities.name: Query protein
observations: The 89-residue sequence exactly matches UniProt Q46971 (Microcin N) from Escherichia coli; sequence identity and coverage are 100%, with E-value 4.53e-43.
Calculated molecular mass is 8,896.058 Da, theoretical pI 6.528, instability index 27.299, GRAVY -0.0135, and predicted charge at pH 7 is -0.4126.
The exact reference annotation classifies it as a secreted, channel-forming microcin active against Escherichia coli and Salmonella; immunity is probably provided by McnI.
GO cellular-component annotation is extracellular region (GO:0005576), based on experimental evidence in the reference record.
No Pfam domain was reported; this negative result is inconclusive because the Pfam module returned no result.

entities.name: Microcin N
observations: UniProt Q46971, Escherichia coli; reviewed Swiss-Prot entry.
A channel-forming microcin with activity against E. coli and Salmonella, but not Listeria or Campylobacter according to cited literature and database annotation.
Likely neutralized by immunity protein McnI.

entities.name: Microcin E492
observations: UniProt Q9Z4N4 from Klebsiella pneumoniae is a related channel-forming bacteriocin with 41.4% identity over 97.8% query coverage.
It forms cation-selective channels and may oligomerize as a homodimer or homotrimer; this is family context, not direct evidence for the exact query protein.

entities.name: McnI
observations: Probable immunity protein for Microcin N, according to the curated Q46971 annotation.
